To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maternal 25(O) vitamin D status during the third trimester is positively related to offspring bone mass, but there is no evidence of a relationship with maternal calcium intake.
maternal 25(OHD) concentrations during pregnancy and maternal calcium intakes during pregnancy are positively associated with offspring bone mass.
maternal vitamin D status in pregnancy is associated with offspring bone mass in later life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel risk factors for osteoporosis and the development of strategies for its prevention, with particular emphasis on early life.
identifying the determinants of bone mass and structure in later life and how they can be influenced by environmental factors in early life.
the effects of maternal calcium and vitamin-D status during pregnancy on offspring bone mass and fracture risk in later life.

the evidence is not yet conclusive, and that more research is needed.
the available data do not support a positive influence of calcium and/or vitamin D intake on offspring bone health.
maternal calcium intake and 25(OH) vitamin D status are important for fetal skeletal development and bone mineralization and that further research in this area is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence base is currently insufficient to inform the public health policy on vitamin D supplementation in pregnant women.
maternal calcium and vitamin d status in pregnancy are important determinants of bone mass in later life.
maternal vitamin D and calcium intake are positively associated with offspring bone mass and that this relationship is independent of maternal bone mineral status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal vitamin D status in pregnancy is an important factor for the offspring bone health.
there is a clear need to improve the quality of data on the role of maternal vitamin D in pregnancy in relation offspring bone health.
